research_concepts: shot mix: three-point attempt rate, rim attempt rate, mean shot distance
methodological_questions: Does the design recover a known-direction personnel effect on shot mix (positive control)?
How should exposure be defined from rotation intervals, and how sparse are five-man units?
How can personnel effects be separated from opponent, matchup, score, clock and fatigue confounds?
How should the design handle the shooter/lineup fixed-effect confound and the mechanical link between who is on the floor and who shoots?
What placebo/negative controls and multiplicity rules apply?

historical_evidence.finding: For the PULL_UP exposure effect, the slope with lineup fixed effects was -0.0255 (0.0061) and without them -0.0063 (0.0036). The same-shooter placebo on other play types was about -0.0075. The record attributes this to a shooter-level confound (risks CONFOUNDING and PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).

When the opposing rim big is off the floor, DRIVE moved +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp, 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), and rim <=4ft +0.12pp (SE 0.295). PPP moved +0.008 (t=+1.1) on N=1.07M possessions. The record's own verdict was weak/small. This concerns opponent lineup, not the team's own five.

The bonus-threshold FTA jump of +5.08pp is the rulebook (mechanical). DRIVE +0.31pp equalled the placebo +0.33pp. The foul-trouble-big condition occurs on only 1.44% of possessions (EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE).
Descriptive play-type mix shifts by half, crunch time and post-run, with no inferential tests. The OTHER label is known to be noisy (LABEL_ERROR, MEASURE_RELIABILITY).

Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels were usable on only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of possessions, and switches_on was unpopulated in the NBA matchups feed. This limits any matchup-scheme covariate.
Inferred defensive-scheme labels cannot separate real adjustment from offense executing differently, and transition matrices were near-uniform, consistent with label noise.

Team-season play-type PPP reliability is low for some types (defensive PPP-allowed 0.173-0.311 for PULL_UP/POST_UP/SPOT_UP), with a median of 472-1,735 possessions per team-season. Play-type-derived outcomes are unreliable at team-season grain.

League-wide exposure slopes were near zero with tight SEs. Only PULL_UP survived Holm correction. The record lists limits of insufficient exposure, label error and low reliability. It is relevant for multiplicity and label handling, not for personnel effects.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading an exposure effect without lineup/shooter fixed effects
failed_approaches.why: The estimate changed substantially with lineup FE and the same-shooter placebo was similar in size, consistent with a shooter-level confound (CONFOUNDING).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a mechanically determined jump as a behavioural effect, and relying on rare exposure
failed_approaches.why: The FTA jump is the rulebook, DRIVE equalled the placebo, and the exposure covered only 1.44% of possessions.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling defensive coverage from NBA matchup/PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Confident labels covered only 3-15% of possessions and switches_on was unpopulated.
They cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive execution, and label noise is consistent with the near-uniform transition matrices.

evidence_establishes: The retrieved records show that this project's earlier shot-mix designs needed placebo and fixed-effect checks to separate real effects from artifacts (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-CHT-076).
The project can estimate sub-1pp to ~2pp shot-mix shifts with SEs of roughly 0.2-0.3pp at about 1M possessions (FAM:SF34), so shifts of that size are resolvable at league scale.
Play-type labels (OTHER) and defensive scheme labels are noisy or sparsely populated (FAM:SF-APPM-021, FAM:SF-APPS-058, FAM:SF-APPA-005).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether changing the team's own offensive five moves shot mix, so nothing answers this question directly.
No retrieved record validates a personnel-change design as a positive control, or gives the size of a known-direction personnel effect.
No retrieved record gives five-man exposure counts or stint-level power.
own_inferences: Shot mix is partly determined by who is on the floor, since individual players have stable shot profiles. A positive result is therefore close to guaranteed and nearly tautological. The informative content lies in the dose-response (observed shift versus the shift predicted from player profiles) and in the placebo contrasts, not in whether any shift is detected.
Defining the 'personnel effect' by shot distance and zone from play-by-play avoids the noisy play-type labels. Using derived play-type records would import LABEL_ERROR.
Single-player swaps with player and team-season fixed effects have far more exposure than unique five-man units. Five-man units are sparse and raise RTM_SELECTION if chosen post hoc.
Substitution timing is endogenous (fatigue, fouls, score, coach response to a cold stretch). Without a window and covariate design this can produce spurious shifts.

The question as phrased ('showing the design can detect personnel effects') risks circular reasoning if 'detect' is defined by any significant shift. A pre-specified directional and magnitude prediction is required.
uncertainties: Exact possession and stint counts per swap type are unknown before analysis.
Whether play-by-play shot distance is accurate enough for zone definitions (for example rim <=4ft) is not recorded in the retrieved evidence.
Whether prior-season shot profiles for rookies, traded players or players with little time are stable enough is unknown.
No power analysis from earlier work applies directly; SF34's SEs come from a different exposure.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record tests the question directly. The earlier artifacts (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-CHT-076) and the label problems moved the decision from a plain 'proceed' to 'proceed_with_changes'. The changes are: require fixed effects, a placebo/negative-control swap, a pre-specified predicted-effect slope rather than a bare significance test, PBP-based shot-location outcomes instead of play-type labels, and a swap-level exposure instead of unique five-man units.

blocking_constraints.text: The question would be circular if the effect were defined using play-type labels derived from the same shots. Use raw PBP shot distance/zone outcomes and player profiles estimated from separate data (prior season or held-out games).

Shot mix follows mechanically from who is on the floor, so a bare 'detects a shift' test cannot fail. A quantitative prediction (observed vs profile-predicted shift) and null swaps are needed for the result to be informative.

prior_work.summary: Retrieved work covers opponent-lineup effects and exposure slopes, not the team's own five. It supplies cautionary artifact lessons (lineup/shooter confound, mechanical floor, placebo dependence) but no direct answer.

risks.text: Substitutions are endogenous to score, clock, foul trouble, fatigue and opponent lineup. Opponent five and matchup composition change at the same time. Model with game, team-season and opponent-lineup controls and use windows around the change.
Different players shoot differently, so a shift is expected by construction. The test must compare observed with predicted shifts and include null swaps.
Unique five-man units are sparse. Use single-player swap stints or player-level on/off with shrinkage, and require a minimum possession count per stint side.

Choosing lineups or swaps after seeing extreme shot mixes yields regression to the mean. Define the swap set from rotation data before looking at outcomes, and estimate player profiles on held-out data.

Earlier work found placebos matching the effect (FAM:SF-CHT-076, FAM:SF-TMP-009). Include negative controls: swaps between players with matched profiles, and pseudo-swap times shifted by a fixed number of possessions.
Play-type labels such as OTHER are noisy (FAM:SF-APPM-021). Define outcomes from PBP shot distance and result only.
Shot-zone shares at stint level are noisy and team-level reliability can be low (FAM:SF-TMP-017). Pool at the possession or shot level with cluster-robust SEs by team-game.
Several shot-mix outcomes and swap types are possible. Pre-register a small primary family and apply Holm correction across it.
Three seasons with league shot-mix trends and player development. Include season fixed effects and test stability by season.

design.estimand: Within team-season, the change in offensive shot mix (share of FGA that are 3PA; share at rim <=4ft; mean shot distance) following a pre-defined change in the offensive five, expressed as the slope of observed shift on the shift predicted from the entering and leaving players' out-of-sample shot profiles. The positive control passes if the slope is positive, its CI excludes 0, and the CI is compatible with a slope near 1 and incompatible with 0.
design.unit: Offensive possession-level shot attempts (or shots within a stint), grouped into swap events defined from the substitution rotation intervals (one-player swaps for the primary analysis), clustered by team-game.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 regular season and playoffs. Primary: regular season; playoffs as a pre-specified secondary stratum. Exclude garbage time (pre-specified score/clock rule), the last 2 minutes of periods, heave attempts and end-of-period possessions. Include only stints with at least a pre-set minimum of possessions on both sides of the swap. Use 2022-23 and 2023-24 for estimating player profiles and 2024-25 for confirmation, or odd/even games within season. Do not choose swaps by outcome.
design.power: No direct power calculation is available from retrieved evidence. Pre-registration step: count eligible swap events and shots before outcomes are viewed, and require a minimum detectable shift in 3PA share of about 1pp at 80% power. SF34 achieved SEs of about 0.25-0.3pp at about 1M possessions, a rough reference only. If the swap count fails the threshold, report untestable for that outcome rather than weakening the threshold.
design.controls: Player and team-season fixed effects, opponent-five or opponent-big presence, score margin, period and clock bins, rest/back-to-back, and home/away. Profiles come from held-out data. Use pre-change windows of matched length and a difference-in-differences against same-game stretches without a change.
design.falsification: (1) Null swaps between players with matched held-out profiles should show a shift near zero. (2) Pseudo-swaps with the change time shifted by a fixed number of possessions without an actual change should show no shift. (3) The predicted-shift slope should not hold for outcomes unrelated to shooting profile (for example free-throw rate given the swap). (4) Compare estimates with and without player fixed effects, since the earlier lineup FE sensitivity was large (FAM:SF-TMP-009).
design.multiplicity: Primary family of three outcomes (3PA share, rim share, mean shot distance) with Holm correction at alpha 0.05. Everything else is exploratory and labelled as such. No play-type outcomes in the primary family.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the predicted-shift slope has a CI above 0 (Holm-adjusted) for at least two of the three outcomes, null swaps and pseudo-swaps are statistically indistinguishable from 0, and results are directionally consistent across seasons. Rejected only if the design has adequate power and the CI for the slope excludes meaningful positive values. Artifact if effects appear in pseudo-swaps or null swaps. Untestable or uncertain otherwise, including when swap counts fall below the power threshold.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 (play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters, box-score summary), as available on 2026-11-02. Freeze the data pull and record version/date. Use no derived play-type graph records for the primary outcomes.

research_concepts: shot mix (shot distance, shot zone, three-point rate, rim attempts)
substitution rotation intervals and five-man units
methodological_questions: Can a design detect shot-mix changes when the offensive five changes (positive control)?
How to define exposure from substitution intervals and handle sparse five-man lineup samples?
How to separate personnel effects from opponent, defensive matchup, game state and score confounding?
How to avoid regression to the mean and selection when lineups are chosen post hoc?
What power, multiple-testing and placebo considerations apply to shot-mix outcomes?
args.query: changing the offensive five moves shot mix; personnel effect detection design as positive control using play-by-play shot distance and substitution rotations

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm wrapping up the final answer now, though I could still call a tool if needed. I'll cite only the returned records and keep their status exactly as recorded. The question is whether changing the offensive five shifts shot mix as a positive control, and none of the retrieved records address that directly; SF34 is only loosely related and shows small, inconclusive shifts.

I'm weighing whether a player-swap design can serve as a positive control, since changing the five obviously changes who takes shots. The more useful check is whether the design's sensitivity can detect a shift of known size, so I'm considering predicting the shot-mix change from the incoming and outgoing players' prior shot profiles and testing whether the observed shift tracks that prediction. A shuffled-lineup placebo would serve as the negative control.

I'm settling on the design details now: a swap-one comparison with player fixed effects, where the predicted shot-mix change comes from the incoming and outgoing players' profiles and a shuffled-lineup placebo serves as the negative control. I'm rating the odds of support fairly high but flagging that the check may be close to tautological, so I'm leaning toward proceeding with changes.
